description: Purbasha Handicrafts and Handloom Centre is an important culture destination in West Tripura district. Good place to explore Tripura's tribal crafts textiles bamboo work and local products.

description: Tribal Museum Agartala is an important museum destination in West Tripura district. Displays the traditions lifestyles material culture and artistic heritage of Tripura's indigenous communities.

name: Laxminarayan Temple
description: Laxminarayan Temple is an important temple destination in West Tripura district. Prominent temple in central Agartala and part of the city's historic religious circuit.

name: Jagannath Temple Agartala
description: Jagannath Temple Agartala is an important temple destination in West Tripura district. Distinctive temple with an octagonal base and elaborate architectural details.

name: Uma Maheswar Temple

name: Benuban Vihar

name: Gedu Mian Mosque
description: Gedu Mian Mosque is an important temple destination in West Tripura district. Historic mosque reflecting Agartala's lesser-known Islamic architectural heritage.

name: Portuguese Church Agartala
description: Portuguese Church Agartala is an important temple destination in West Tripura district. Historic Christian landmark showing the religious diversity of Agartala.

name: Fourteen Goddess Temple Khayerpur
description: Fourteen Goddess Temple Khayerpur is an important temple destination in West Tripura district. Major Tripura shrine dedicated to the Fourteen Gods and connected with the Kharchi tradition.

name: Kharchi Temple Complex
description: Kharchi Temple Complex is an important temple destination in West Tripura district. Temple complex and festival landscape central to Tripura's royal and indigenous traditions.

description: Nagicherra Rubber Wood Processing Centre is an important agri tourism destination in West Tripura district. Working industrial and craft-oriented attraction showcasing rubber wood processing.

name: Durgabari Tea Garden
description: Durgabari Tea Garden is an important agri tourism destination in West Tripura district. Tea estate landscape close to Agartala providing a green rural contrast to the capital.

name: Capital Complex Agartala
description: Capital Complex Agartala is an important nature destination in West Tripura district. Government and civic architecture representing modern Tripura's capital landscape.

name: Agartala old city lanes
description: Agartala old city lanes is an important heritage destination in West Tripura district. Historic streets around the palace and temple zone reveal layers of royal-era urban development.

name: Agartala craft markets
description: Agartala craft markets is an important culture destination in West Tripura district. Local markets provide access to bamboo cane textiles tribal handicrafts and regional products.

name: Agartala cultural circuit
description: Agartala cultural circuit is an important heritage destination in West Tripura district. Compact combination of palace museums temples parks crafts and historic institutions.

name: Ranirbazar local heritage
description: Ranirbazar local heritage is an important nature destination in West Tripura district. Small-town setting useful for exploring local markets and rural culture away from Agartala's tourist core.

name: Montang Valley (Mountain of Peace)
description: A scenic, cloud-draped hill valley located along the Atharamura range, characterized by open rolling pastures, bamboo watch platforms, and morning mist inversions.

name: Saika (Tuisoi) Waterfall
description: A multi-tiered forest cascade tucked away inside deep subtropical woodland near the border foothills, reached via quiet village hiking paths.

name: Narkel Kunja (Coconut Island) Outer Bends
description: While the central island is becoming known, the untouched mangrove-like fingers and uninhabited islets across the northern Dumboor lake reservoir offer remote boat trails and quiet waterbird watching.

name: Longtharai Sacred Ridge & Valley Trails
description: Ancestral hill trails sacred to the Kokborok-speaking indigenous communities, winding through deep ravines, bamboo thickets, and Shiva shrines.

name: Tirthamukh Confluence (Raima-Sarma Meeting Point)
description: A tranquil river junction and hydro-reservoir head where the Raima and Sarma rivers converge to form the Gomati River, flanked by forested hills and sacred bathing ghats.

name: Amar Sagar & Fatik Sagar Dighi Bunds
description: Massive 16th-century man-made reservoirs commissioned by the Manikya rulers in Amarpur, surrounded by palace ruins, ancient banyans, and quiet sunset walks.

name: Tepania Eco Park Buffer Trails
description: Shaded forest walking trails and high wooden watchtowers nestled inside dense natural dipterocarp and bamboo groves near Udaipur.

name: Baramura Eco Park & Hornbill Trail
description: A protected evergreen sanctuary across the Baramura (Hathai Kotor) range, featuring wooden canopy walks, bamboo suspension footbridges, and wild forest bird habitats.

name: Khowai River Shallows & Sandy Reaches
description: Unpaved riverbed tracks and pebbled bends where clear foothill waters carve through rural tea gardens and agricultural plains.

name: Padmabil & Chakmaghat Barrage Backwaters
description: A quiet irrigation reservoir framed by low-lying hillocks, offering peaceful shorelines for seasonal migratory birding.

name: Baisnabpur Tea Estate Trails
description: Undulating organic green tea gardens situated along the foothills, retaining quiet colonial plantation tracks and scenic sunset views.

name: Shilchhara Buddha Waterfall
description: A tucked-away forest cascade flowing through rocky sandstone ledges near a small Buddhist rural enclave.

name: Thaidawr & Vanghmun Trails (Jampui Hills Fringe)
description: Beyond the main Jampui ridge viewpoints, these quiet Mizo hamlets offer orchid-lined garden paths, traditional wooden stilt homes, and sweeping panoramas toward the Mizoram border.

name: Kanchanpur Stream Crossings
description: Calm mountain brooks, orange orchards, and bamboo hanging bridges cutting through the rural northern valleys.

name: Sepahijala Sanctuary Inner Forest Core
description: Beyond the roadside zoo lies an untouched moist-deciduous forest sanctuary sheltering the endangered Phayre’s leaf monkey (spectacled langur) and natural rubber plantations.

name: Abhirampur & Amrit Sagar Lakeside Trails
description: Quiet freshwater lake edges tucked inside rural rubber and agarwood estates, visited mainly by local anglers.

name: Kasba Kalibari (Kamalasagar Border Shoreline)
description: An ancient 15th-century hilltop Kali temple perched on the edge of a vast medieval water tank (Kamalasagar), looking directly across the barbed-wire border into the flat plains of Bangladesh.

name: Boxanagar Archaeological Mound Outer Trenches
description: The peaceful excavated brick ruins of a 6th–8th century post-Gupta Buddhist stupa, monastery, and chaitya hall hidden inside village farmland.

name: Muhuri Char (Belonia River Edge)
description: A quiet riverine sandbar on the Muhuri River along the international border, offering calm waters and views of seasonal mustard and paddy fields.

name: Unakoti Hill Back-Ridge & Forest Springs
description: While the main 30-foot monolithic bas-relief of Unakotishwara Kal Bhairava draws pilgrims, the upper mossy rock trails leading to natural seasonal cascades and forest rock alcoves remain quiet and untamed.

name: Kailashahar Royal Rajbari Grounds
description: The understated historical ruins of the old royal headquarters of the Manikya kings, surrounded by heritage tea gardens and ancient temple tanks.

name: Kalacherra Eco Park
description: A peaceful green woodland park bordering running mountain streams, frequented almost exclusively by local picnickers and birders.

name: Pecharthal Buddhist Monastic Groves
description: A quiet village hermitage housing a traditional pagoda, golden Buddha sculptures, and peaceful walking courtyards flanked by rural hamlets.

name: Baramura Hill Waterfalls (Hathai Kotor Range)
description: Hidden seasonal cascades carving through rocky sandstone gorges within the forested interior tracks off NH-8.

name: Brahmapukhur & Champaknagar Heritage Shrines
description: Quiet countryside hillock shrines and centuries-old excavated water ponds set against scenic rubber-estate terraces.

name: Kunjaban Palace Hillock & Heritage Gardens
description: An understated royal retreat built in 1917 by Maharaja Birendra Kishore Manikya, featuring quiet pine terraces and landscaped lawns away from the city center.

name: Howrah River Upper Stream Bends
description: Peaceful, slow-moving river shallows and gravel flats upstream from Agartala, flanked by bamboo groves and traditional farming hamlets.
